column1: # Agent dispatch-guard decision table — <decision><TAB><subagent_type><TAB><isolation><TAB><nested><TAB><desc>.
# decision is block (exit 2) / advise (exit 0, additionalContext) / fallthrough
# (exit 0, no output). Tab-separated; # and blank lines ignored. '-' marks an
# absent isolation/nested value — never a truly empty field between tabs, since
# a whitespace IFS collapses runs of empty fields (the exact bug the guard's own
# jq-to-read split works around; see agent-dispatch-guard.sh).
# The runner fixes one roster for the whole table: DELEGATION_KIT_READONLY_TYPES=(ro-type).
# A subagent_type prefixed 'noroster:' runs with no roster config at all (an
# empty declare), proving D2 stays inert on the roster's absence rather than on
# this type's absence from a populated one; the prefix is stripped before it
# reaches the guard's payload. subagent_type UNPARSEABLE sends invalid JSON on
# stdin instead of a built payload.
# D1 — the fork ban is unconditional
block
column5: a fork dispatch blocks regardless of isolation or roster

column1: fallthrough
column5: a typed, non-fork dispatch is not blocked (no roster configured)

column1: # D2 — a declared read-only type without isolation: worktree
block
column5: a rostered type dispatched without isolation: worktree blocks

column1: fallthrough
column5: the same rostered type with isolation: worktree does not block

column1: fallthrough
column5: a typed dispatch outside a populated roster does not block

column1: fallthrough
column5: D2 stays inert against an empty roster, even naming the type that would otherwise match

column1: # D3 — nested-dispatch advisory (never blocks)
advise
column5: a payload carrying agent_id advises: this dispatch creates a grandchild

column1: fallthrough
column5: a payload with no agent_id falls through D3 untouched

column1: # Degradation — fail-open, but loud
advise
column5: an unparseable payload advises rather than blocks, naming what could not be enforced
